name: Assam
summary_text: Assam recorded 2 of the 7 national Transgender Persons Act cases in 2021, indicating some functioning legal infrastructure for trans-related complaints. The state is part of the Northeast border belt where the infiltration/Bangladeshi-detention script operates — the Panisagar raids ran along the Assam–Agartala highway — though no Assam-specific checkpoint case was identified in this research pass. Assam has NOT constituted a transgender welfare board: per the official 12-board list (Dec 2021) it is among the states/UTs still lacking one. Against the national 0.43, Assam sits marginally +0.02. The positive signal is thin: recorded cases could indicate either crimes happening or a legal system engaging with them, and the dossier frames the latter reading. The negative ambient signal (proximity to the Tripura/West Bengal border-profiling zone) is not offset by any Assam-specific protective policy comparable to Tamil Nadu or Kerala, and the missing welfare board marks lower official visibility than in the southern states. Compared to West Bengal (0.34), Assam shares the border-belt exposure but lacks the documented trans-as-infiltration arrests; compared to Tripura (0.31), the absence of any named checkpoint operation in Assam is the key differentiator. The deviation is small and confidence is low.

sources.title: India’s crime data would have you believe that trans people barely face any violence—here’s why that doesn’t add up - Queerbeat
sources.claim_summary: queerbeat data report (30 Jan 2026): per the NCRB, the Transgender Persons Act recorded only 20 cases nationwide 2019-2023 - 1 in Tamil Nadu (2020); 7 in 2021 (2 each in Assam and Kerala, 3 in West Bengal); 1 in Tamil Nadu (2022); 11 in 2023 (7 Tamil Nadu, 4 Kerala), none from north and central India; it attributes the scarcity to police registration bias, against survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence (2025 Transgender Health study, n=4,964).

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau reply in the Rajya Sabha (8 Dec 2021, Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar): 12 states/UTs have constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
